rationale:
The supplied proof of dtc_cone_of_constant_density consists of two independent halves that meet only in the radial-tangency property "x ∈ T_xM for μ_C-a.e. x". (A) Analytic half, parent steps 0–4: AE-measurability of the tangent-projection field, Simon's stationary monotonicity identity 4.3.6, and D^⊥r = 0 when the ball ratio is constant. (B) Homotopy half, steps 5–7: x ∧ C⃗ = 0, Cartan's formula for the Euler field, and Simon's cone criterion, Lemma 6.2.33.

Each child is a genuine reusable named obligation:
(1) tangent_projection_measurable: x ↦ p_{T_xM} is AEMeasurable for every IMRep (Cauchy–Binet, step 0).
(2) monotonicity_identity: Simon 4.3.6 for v(M,θ) in ℝ^P (step 3).
(3) radial_tangency: a constant ratio μ(B_ρ(0)) = aρⁿ forces p_x x = x μ-a.e. (steps 1 and 4; the parent's use of μ({0}) = 0 is replaced by p_0(0) = 0, so n ≥ 1 is not needed).
(4) wedge_vanishes: radial tangency gives x ∧ ξ = 0 μ-a.e. (step 5).
(5) euler_cartan: d(ι_Xβ) + ι_X dβ = (m+1)β + Dβ[y] for X(y) = y (step 6, algebraic core).
(6) cone_lemma: Simon 6.2.33 for IMRep-represented currents in ℝ^P, i.e. dominated differentiation of s ↦ C(h_s^#ω) plus the blowUp/currentEval translation (steps 6–7).

Proof of the selected theorem from the children:

2. tangentSpace univ y contains every v (take γ(t) = y + tv), so the hypothesis R.IsStationaryAlong univ gives R.firstVariation X = 0 for every C¹ compactly supported X.

subproblems.title: Measurability of the approximate-tangent projection of an integer multiplicity triple (Cauchy–Binet)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple of dimension n in U (IMRep U n). For x ∈ ℝ^P let T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x: the approximate tangent n-plane of M at x when one exists (it is then unique), and {0} otherwise. Let p_x : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be the orthogonal projection onto T_x (starProjection). Then x ↦ p_x ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) is almost-everywhere measurable (AEMeasurable, Borel σ-algebra) with respect to Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), AEMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Sources.
- Parent step 0: the Cauchy–Binet description of the tangent projection through the orientation.
- Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–752): ξ is Hⁿ-measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, ξ(x) = τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space T_xM.
- Simon Ch. 6, 1.5–1.7 (lines 93–108): the induced inner products for which the basic (co)vectors are orthonormal. Step 3 below is the identity behind this.
- Simon Ch. 3, 1.4–1.5 (chapter-03.txt lines 75–90): approximate tangent space, unique if it exists.

Notation. M = R.carrier, ξ = R.orient, ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ⟨e_i, u⟩ = u(i). T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x and p_x is its starProjection. For a subspace Q, p_Q denotes the orthogonal projection onto Q. For b ∈ Fin n, succAbove_b : Fin (n−1) → Fin n is the order embedding that skips b.

1. Case n = 0. Suppose some Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M x Q. Then the subspace Q₀ chosen in the definition of approxTangentPlane also satisfies it, so finrank Q₀ = 0 (first conjunct of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt) and Q₀ = ⊥. Otherwise T_x = ⊥ by definition. Hence p_x = p_⊥ = 0 for every x; a constant function is measurable. From now on n = m + 1.

2. Covectors.
- For j : Fin m → Fin P, let e^j be the m-covector e^j(u_1, …, u_m) := det(u_c(j(r)))_{r,c ∈ Fin m}; for m = 0 it is the constant 1. It is multilinear, alternating and continuous. In SimonGMT it is wedgeCovectors m (fun r ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (j r)); see wedgeCovectors_apply_det in Chapter06/FormsDuality.lean.
- For v ∈ ℝ^P, let α_{v,j} be the n-covector α_{v,j}(u_0, …, u_m) := Σ_{b=0}^{m} (−1)^b ⟨v, u_b⟩ e^j(u_0, …, û_b, …, u_m). Equivalently, α_{v,j} = alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight e^j) = wedgeCovectors n (Fin.cons (innerSL ℝ v) (fun r ↦ proj (j r))).

3. Gram identity (Cauchy–Binet). For a, b : Fin m → ℝ^P,
 Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin P} e^j(a)·e^j(b) = m!·det(⟨a_r, b_c⟩)_{r,c}.
Proof.
(i) By the Leibniz formula applied to the transpose, e^j(a) = Σ_{σ∈S_m} sgn σ Π_r a_{σ(r)}(j(r)) and e^j(b) = Σ_{π∈S_m} sgn π Π_r b_{π(r)}(j(r)).
(ii) Hence Σ_j e^j(a)e^j(b) = Σ_{σ,π} sgn σ sgn π Σ_j Π_r a_{σ(r)}(j(r)) b_{π(r)}(j(r)).
(iii) A sum over all functions j of a product of factors, the r-th depending only on j(r), equals the product of the sums. So the expression is Σ_{σ,π} sgn σ sgn π Π_r Σ_{i=1}^{P} a_{σ(r)}(i) b_{π(r)}(i).
(iv) By Parseval in the standard basis this is Σ_{σ,π} sgn σ sgn π Π_r ⟨a_{σ(r)}, b_{π(r)}⟩.
(v) Substitute r = σ⁻¹(c) in the product. It becomes Π_c ⟨a_c, b_{ρ(c)}⟩ with ρ := π∘σ⁻¹, and sgn σ sgn π = sgn ρ because sgn is multiplicative with values ±1.
(vi) For fixed σ, π ↦ ρ is a bijection of S_m. So the sum is Σ_σ Σ_ρ sgn ρ Π_c ⟨a_c, b_{ρ(c)}⟩ = m!·det((⟨a_r, b_c⟩)ᵀ) = m!·det(⟨a_r, b_c⟩).

4. Projection formula. Let Q be a subspace and ζ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) = (Covector (ℝ^P) n →L ℝ) with IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q. That is, there are an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q and ε ∈ {1, −1} such that ζ(α) = ε·α(τ) for every α. Then for all v, w ∈ ℝ^P,
 Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin P} ζ(α_{v,j})·ζ(α_{w,j}) = m!·⟨p_Q v, w⟩.
Proof.
(i) Deleting the b-th entry of τ gives τ∘succAbove_b. Hence ζ(α_{v,j}) = ε Σ_b (−1)^b ⟨v, τ_b⟩ e^j(τ∘succAbove_b).
(ii) Multiply the expressions for v and w, sum over j, use ε² = 1, and apply step 3 with a = τ∘succAbove_b and b = τ∘succAbove_{b'}:
 Σ_j ζ(α_{v,j})ζ(α_{w,j}) = Σ_{b,b'∈Fin n} (−1)^{b+b'} ⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_{b'}⟩·m!·det(⟨τ_{succAbove_b(r)}, τ_{succAbove_{b'}(c)}⟩)_{r,c}.
(iii) If b = b', the matrix is the identity (τ is orthonormal and succAbove_b is injective), so its determinant is 1.
(iv) If b ≠ b', then b' = succAbove_b(r₀) for some r₀, since succAbove_b is a bijection of Fin m onto Fin n ∖ {b}. Row r₀ of the matrix is (⟨τ_{b'}, τ_{succAbove_{b'}(c)}⟩)_c = 0, because succAbove_{b'}(c) ≠ b'. So the determinant is 0.
(v) Hence the sum is m!·Σ_b ⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_b⟩ = m!·⟨Σ_b ⟨τ_b, v⟩τ_b, w⟩ = m!·⟨p_Q v, w⟩. The last equality holds because (τ_b) is an orthonormal basis of Q, so p_Q v = Σ_b ⟨τ_b, v⟩τ_b.

5. A continuous Π. Define Π : Λ_n(ℝ^P) → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) by
 Π(ζ) := Σ_{a,b=1}^{P} g_{ab}(ζ)·L_{ab},
where g_{ab}(ζ) := (1/m!) Σ_j ζ(α_{e_a,j})·ζ(α_{e_b,j}) and L_{ab}(v) := ⟨e_a, v⟩e_b, i.e. L_{ab} = (innerSL e_a).smulRight e_b.
- For each fixed α, the map ζ ↦ ζ(α) is continuous and linear. Hence each g_{ab} is continuous, and so is Π.
- If IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q, then g_{ab}(ζ) = ⟨p_Q e_a, e_b⟩ by step 4. So for all v: Π(ζ)v = Σ_b Σ_a ⟨e_a, v⟩⟨p_Q e_a, e_b⟩e_b = Σ_b ⟨p_Q(Σ_a ⟨e_a,v⟩e_a), e_b⟩e_b = Σ_b ⟨p_Q v, e_b⟩e_b = p_Q v. That is, Π(ζ) = p_Q.

6. A.e. identification. By the field `orients`, for ν-a.e. x there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x. At such x, the condition of the `if` in approxTangentPlane holds. The chosen subspace Q' then satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q', and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (SimonGMT, Ch. 3 Remark 1.5(1)) gives Q' = Q_x. So T_x = Q_x and, by step 5, p_x = Π(ξ x).

7. Conclusion. ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient) and Π is continuous, so Π∘ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν. By step 6, x ↦ p_x equals Π∘ξ ν-a.e., so it is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν. It is therefore AEMeasurable for the Borel σ-algebra of the finite-dimensional normed space L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P). ∎
proof_key_steps: n = 0: approxTangentPlane is ⊥ everywhere, so the projection is the constant 0.
Gram (Cauchy–Binet) identity Σ_{j:Fin m→Fin P} e^j(a)e^j(b) = m!·det(⟨a_r,b_c⟩), by Leibniz expansion, product-of-sums and Parseval.
If ζ = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ orients Q, then Σ_j ζ(v♭∧e^j)ζ(w♭∧e^j) = m!⟨p_Q v, w⟩; this defines a continuous Π with Π(ζ) = p_Q.
Hⁿ-a.e. on M, ξ(x) orients the unique approximate tangent plane T_x, so p_x = Π(ξ(x)); composing the continuous Π with the AE-strongly-measurable ξ gives AEMeasurable.

subproblems.title: Stationary monotonicity identity (Simon 4.3.6) for the varifold of an IMRep in ℝ^P
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n), with μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For x ∈ ℝ^P let p_x be the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x. Suppose V = v(M, θ) is stationary in ℝ^P in the computed sense: R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ·trace(p_x∘DX(x)) dHⁿ = 0 for every C¹ vector field X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support. Then for every z ∈ ℝ^P and 0 < σ ≤ ρ, with B̄ denoting closed balls and the identity taken in [0, ∞] (written with ENNReal.ofReal),
 μ(B̄_σ(z))/σⁿ + ∫_{B̄_ρ(z)∖B̄_σ(z)} |(x−z) − p_x(x−z)|² / |x−z|^{n+2} dμ(x) = μ(B̄_ρ(z))/ρⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ X : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → R.firstVariation X = 0) → ∀ (z : Euclid P) (σ ρ : ℝ), 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → R.measure (closedBall z σ) / ENNReal.ofReal (σ ^ n) + ∫⁻ x in closedBall z ρ \ closedBall z σ, ENNReal.ofReal (‖(x - z) - (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection (x - z)‖ ^ 2 / ‖x - z‖ ^ (n + 2)) ∂R.measure = R.measure (closedBall z ρ) / ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Sources. Simon Ch. 4, 3.1–3.6 (chapter-04.txt lines 212–312; Simon's B_ρ are closed balls), applied with U = ℝ^P, R = ∞ and centre z. This is step 3 of the parent proof, with its step 0 for integrability. It is formalized in SimonGMT as Chapter04.RectifiableVarifold.IsStationaryIn.satisfiesStationaryMonotonicity. Uses sibling tangent_projection_measurable (child 1).

Notation. M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ν := Hⁿ⌞M, μ = R.measure = ν.withDensity θ. T_x = approxTangentPlane n M x and p_x is its orthogonal projection. r(x) := |x − z| and B̄_t := closedBall(z, t). For x ≠ z, D^⊥r(x) := (x−z)/r − p_x((x−z)/r). Then |D^⊥r|²r^{−n} = |(x−z) − p_x(x−z)|²/|x−z|^{n+2} and |D^⊥r| ≤ 1.

0. Preliminaries.
(a) For compact K, μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞, by locallyIntegrable_mult with K ⊆ ℝ^P = U (K is closed, hence Borel).
(b) μ ≪ ν. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, a property holds μ-a.e. iff it holds ν-a.e.
(c) By `orients`, for ν-a.e. x some Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. By the definition of approxTangentPlane and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, at such x we have HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x T_x and dim T_x = n.
(d) x ↦ p_x is ν-AEMeasurable (child 1), hence μ-AEMeasurable by (b).
(e) Let X ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) and div_M X(x) := trace(p_x∘DX(x)).
 - div_M X is μ-AEMeasurable by (d).
 - |div_M X(x)| ≤ P·‖DX(x)‖: expand the trace in an orthonormal basis and use ‖p_x‖ ≤ 1.
 - Since ‖DX‖ is continuous with compact support, (a) makes div_M X μ-integrable.
 - R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ·div_M X dHⁿ = ∫ div_M X dμ (integration against a measurable ℕ-valued density).
 So the hypothesis is the genuine identity ∫ div_M X dμ = 0 for every X ∈ C¹_c.

1. Radial test fields (Simon 3.1–3.3). Let γ ∈ C¹(ℝ) with γ' = 0 on (−∞, δ] for some δ > 0 and γ = 0 on [T, ∞).
- X(x) := γ(r(x))(x − z) is C¹ with compact support; it equals γ(0)(x − z) on B_δ(z).
- For x ≠ z, DX(x)u = γ(r)u + γ'(r)⟨(x−z)/r, u⟩(x−z).
- For μ-a.e. x (those with dim T_x = n), trace(p_x) = n. Also, by Pythagoras, trace(p_x∘(u ↦ ⟨(x−z)/r, u⟩(x−z))) = ⟨p_x(x−z), (x−z)/r⟩ = r|p_x((x−z)/r)|² = r(1 − |D^⊥r|²).
- Hence div_M X = nγ(r) + rγ'(r)(1 − |D^⊥r|²). At x = z both sides equal nγ(0).
- By (e): n∫γ(r)dμ + ∫rγ'(r)dμ = ∫rγ'(r)|D^⊥r|²dμ (Simon 3.3).

2. Cutoff (Simon 3.4). Fix ε ∈ (0,1) and a nonincreasing φ = φ_ε ∈ C¹(ℝ; [0,1]) with φ = 1 on (−∞, 1] and φ = 0 on [1+ε, ∞) (e.g. SimonGMT monotonicityCutoff). For t > 0 take γ(r) := φ(r/t) in step 1, and put I(t) := ∫φ(r/t)dμ and J(t) := ∫φ(r/t)|D^⊥r|²dμ (finite by (a)).
- We have rγ'(r) = (r/t)φ'(r/t) = −t∂_t[φ(r/t)].
- ∂_tφ(r/t) = −(r/t²)φ'(r/t) is bounded by (1+ε)sup|φ'|/t and supported in B̄_{(1+ε)t}, uniformly for t in compact subsets of (0, ∞). So differentiation under the integral sign is justified.
- Step 1 then gives nI(t) − tI'(t) = −tJ'(t), i.e. d/dt(t^{−n}I(t)) = t^{−n}J'(t) for t > 0.

3. Squeeze (Simon 3.5, with the prefactors in the correct order). Let 0 < σ < ρ.
- Integrate step 2 over [σ, ρ] and use Fubini (∂_tφ(r/t) ≥ 0): ρ^{−n}I(ρ) − σ^{−n}I(σ) = ∫(∫_σ^ρ t^{−n}∂_tφ(r/t)dt)|D^⊥r|²dμ.
- ∂_tφ(r/t) ≠ 0 only when r/(1+ε) < t < r, and there r^{−n} ≤ t^{−n} ≤ (1+ε)ⁿr^{−n}.
- ∫_σ^ρ ∂_tφ(r/t)dt = φ(r/ρ) − φ(r/σ) ≥ 0, and it vanishes where r ≤ σ (both values are 1).
- Hence ∫r^{−n}(φ(r/ρ) − φ(r/σ))|D^⊥r|²dμ ≤ ρ^{−n}I(ρ) − σ^{−n}I(σ) ≤ (1+ε)ⁿ∫r^{−n}(φ(r/ρ) − φ(r/σ))|D^⊥r|²dμ, and all integrals are finite.

4. Limit ε ↓ 0 (Simon 3.6).
- φ_ε(s) → 1_{(−∞,1]}(s) for every s: for s > 1, φ_ε(s) = 0 once 1 + ε < s. So φ_ε(r/t) → 1_{B̄_t} pointwise, dominated by 1_{B̄_{2t}}, which is μ-integrable by (a).
- Likewise r^{−n}(φ_ε(r/ρ) − φ_ε(r/σ))|D^⊥r|² → r^{−n}|D^⊥r|²·1_{B̄_ρ∖B̄_σ}, dominated by σ^{−n}1_{B̄_{2ρ}}.
- Dominated convergence in step 3, with (1+ε)ⁿ → 1, gives
 ρ^{−n}μ(B̄_ρ) − σ^{−n}μ(B̄_σ) = ∫_{B̄_ρ∖B̄_σ} |D^⊥r|²r^{−n}dμ for 0 < σ < ρ.
- For σ = ρ both sides are 0.

5. Conclusion. On B̄_ρ∖B̄_σ we have x ≠ z and |D^⊥r|²r^{−n} = |(x−z) − p_x(x−z)|²/|x−z|^{n+2} ≥ 0. All quantities are finite and nonnegative. Move σ^{−n}μ(B̄_σ) to the right-hand side and apply ENNReal.ofReal:
- ofReal is additive on nonnegative reals;
- ofReal of the integral of a nonnegative integrable function is the lower integral of ofReal;
- ofReal(μ(B̄_t)/tⁿ) = μ(B̄_t)/ofReal(tⁿ), since μ(B̄_t) < ∞.
This gives exactly
 μ(B̄_σ(z))/ofReal(σⁿ) + ∫⁻_{B̄_ρ(z)∖B̄_σ(z)} ofReal(|(x−z) − p_x(x−z)|²/|x−z|^{n+2}) dμ = μ(B̄_ρ(z))/ofReal(ρⁿ). ∎

Implementation note. During decomposition this exact statement was proved in Lean from the exact statement of child 1 (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). Steps 1–4 are SimonGMT's RectifiableVarifold.IsStationaryIn.satisfiesStationaryMonotonicity; import Chapter04/FirstVariation.lean and Chapter04/MultiplicityBridge.lean in the submission.
- Build V : Chapter04.RectifiableVarifold n with carrier M, multiplicity x ↦ (θ x : ℝ) and tangent := approxTangentPlane n M.
 - approximate_tangent: from (c).
 - multiplicity_hypotheses and locallyFiniteWeight: from (a).
 - tangentProjection_aemeasurable := (child 1).mono_ac, using withDensity_indicator and withDensity_absolutelyContinuous.
- V.weight = R.measure, by weight_eq_carrier_withDensity and ENNReal.ofReal_natCast.
- V.IsStationaryIn univ: from the hypothesis via integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul (density x ↦ (θ x : ℝ≥0)) and LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'.
- Apply satisfiesStationaryMonotonicity with outer radius ρ + 1 and unfold normalizedBallMass and monotonicityDefect.
- On the annulus, rewrite V.radialNormalSq z x/‖x−z‖ⁿ into the integrand above (radialNormalSq_eq, norm_smul, field_simp, setLIntegral_congr_fun).
proof_key_steps: Child 1 and θ ≥ 1 make div_M X = trace(p_x∘DX) μ-integrable, so the hypothesis reads ∫ div_M X dμ = 0 for every X ∈ C¹_c.
Radial fields X = φ(r/t)(x−z) give div_M X = nφ + (r/t)φ'(1 − |D^⊥r|²), hence d/dt(t^{−n}I(t)) = t^{−n}J'(t) (Simon 4.3.2–3.4).
Integrating over [σ,ρ], the squeeze r^{−n} ≤ t^{−n} ≤ (1+ε)ⁿr^{−n} and dominated convergence as ε ↓ 0 give Simon 4.3.6 on closed balls.
Rewrite in [0,∞] with the integrand |(x−z) − p_x(x−z)|²/|x−z|^{n+2}; in Lean, bridge to SimonGMT satisfiesStationaryMonotonicity through a RectifiableVarifold with weight R.measure.

subproblems.title: Constant ball-mass ratio forces radial tangency x ∈ T_xM a.e. (Simon 7.3.1 proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) with R.firstVariation X = 0 for every C¹ compactly supported X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Suppose there is a ∈ [0, ∞] with μ(B_ρ(0)) = a·ρⁿ (as a * ofReal(ρⁿ)) for every ρ > 0, where μ = R.measure and B_ρ is the open ball. Then p_x(x) = x, i.e. x ∈ approxTangentPlane n M x, for μ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P (p_x being the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (a : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ X : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → R.firstVariation X = 0) → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → R.measure (ball 0 ρ) = a * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection x = x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Proof of Simon 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 343–358): "(ω_nρⁿ)⁻¹μ_C(B_ρ(0)) = Θⁿ(T, x) for each ρ > 0. Then by the monotonicity formula 3.6 of Ch. 4 … we have D^⊥r = 0 μ_C-a.e. … That is x ∈ T_x spt C for μ_C-a.e. x." These are steps 1 and 4 of the parent proof. Uses siblings tangent_projection_measurable (child 1) and monotonicity_identity (child 2).

Notation. μ := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, and p_x := starProjection of approxTangentPlane n M x. B_ρ and B̄_ρ are the open and closed balls about 0.

1. Local finiteness. For compact K, μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult with U = ℝ^P; withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict on the closed set K).

2. a < ∞. Indeed a = a·ofReal(1ⁿ) = μ(B_1) ≤ μ(B̄_1) < ∞.

3. Closed balls. Fix ρ > 0.
- μ(B̄_ρ) ≥ μ(B_ρ) = a·ofReal(ρⁿ).
- For every t > ρ, B̄_ρ ⊆ B_t, so μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ a·ofReal(tⁿ).
- Since a < ∞, t ↦ a·ofReal(tⁿ) is continuous; letting t ↓ ρ gives μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ a·ofReal(ρⁿ).
Hence μ(B̄_ρ) = a·ofReal(ρⁿ). As 0 < ofReal(ρⁿ) < ∞, the normalized ratio is μ(B̄_ρ)/ofReal(ρⁿ) = a.

4. Annuli. Let 0 < σ ≤ ρ, A(σ,ρ) := B̄_ρ ∖ B̄_σ and f(x) := |x − p_x x|²/|x|^{n+2}. Child 2 with z = 0, together with step 3, gives a + D(σ,ρ) = a, where D(σ,ρ) := ∫⁻_{A(σ,ρ)} ofReal(f) dμ. Since a < ∞, D(σ,ρ) = 0.

5. Measurability and pointwise vanishing.
- x ↦ p_x is μ-AEMeasurable: by child 1, and μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
- Evaluation (L, v) ↦ Lv is continuous, hence Borel. So x ↦ p_x x is μ-AEMeasurable, and so are f and ofReal∘f.
- Therefore D(σ,ρ) = 0 gives ofReal(f(x)) = 0, i.e. f(x) ≤ 0, for μ-a.e. x ∈ A(σ,ρ).
- On A(σ,ρ) we have |x| > σ > 0, so |x − p_x x|² ≤ 0, i.e. p_x x = x.

6. Exhaustion.
- Let A_k := A(1/(k+1), k+1) for k ∈ ℕ (note 1/(k+1) ≤ k+1).
- By step 5 and countable intersection of a.e. statements, for μ-a.e. x: for every k, x ∈ A_k implies p_x x = x.
- Every x ≠ 0 lies in A_k as soon as k > max(|x|, 1/|x|).
- For x = 0, p_0(0) = 0 by linearity.
Hence p_x x = x for μ-a.e. x. Neither n ≥ 1 nor μ({0}) = 0 is needed. ∎

Implementation note. During decomposition this exact statement was proved in Lean from the exact statements of children 1 and 2, with standard axioms only. Key lemmas: withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, ge_of_tendsto with ENNReal.continuousAt_const_mul, ENNReal.mul_div_cancel_right, ENNReal.add_right_inj, lintegral_eq_zero_iff', ae_restrict_iff', ContinuousLinearMap.measurable_apply₂, ae_all_iff.
proof_key_steps: Local finiteness forces a < ∞; squeezing between open balls gives μ(B̄_ρ(0)) = aρⁿ, so the normalized ratio is constantly a.
Child 2 at z = 0 then forces the defect ∫_{annulus}|x − p_x x|²|x|^{−n−2} dμ to vanish.
Child 1 makes the integrand measurable, so p_x x = x μ-a.e. on every annulus.
Countably many annuli exhaust ℝ^P∖{0}; p_0(0) = 0 handles the origin.

subproblems.title: Radial tangency gives x ∧ C⃗ = 0 a.e. (Simon 7.3.1 proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(U, n) such that p_x(x) = x for R.measure-a.e. x, where p_x is the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x. Then for R.measure-a.e. x and every (n+1)-covector β on ℝ^P, ξ(x)(ι_xβ) = 0. Here ι_xβ = ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β x is the n-covector (v₁,…,vₙ) ↦ β(x, v₁, …, vₙ). This is Simon's 'x ∧ C⃗ = 0 μ_C-a.e.'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), (∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection x = x) → ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1), R.orient x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β x) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Sources.
- Proof of Simon 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 358–359): "That is x ∈ T_x spt C for μ_C-a.e. x, so in particular x ∧ C⃗ = 0 μ_C-a.e." This is step 5 of the parent proof.
- Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–742): ξ(x) = τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM.

Notation. M = R.carrier, ξ = R.orient, μ = R.measure. T_x = approxTangentPlane n M x and p_x is its starProjection. ι_xβ := ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β x, so (ι_xβ)(v_1, …, v_n) = β(x, v_1, …, v_n).

1. Choosing good points. μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, so the Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. property `orients` also holds μ-a.e. Together with the hypothesis: for μ-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q, and also p_x x = x. Fix such an x and an (n+1)-covector β.

2. x ∈ Q. The `if` in approxTangentPlane is satisfied (witness Q). The chosen subspace Q' satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q', and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique gives Q' = Q. So T_x = Q and p_Q x = x. An orthogonal projection fixes exactly the vectors of its range (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff), so x ∈ Q.

3. Orientation data. IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q means: there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q, and either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α.

4. Vanishing on Q.
- The map y ↦ (ι_yβ)(τ) = β(y, τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) is linear in y, because curryLeft β is a continuous linear map.
- For y = τ_b, the (n+1)-tuple (τ_b, τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) has equal entries at the distinct positions 0 and b+1. Since β is alternating, β vanishes on it.
- Hence the linear map vanishes on span(range τ) = Q (span induction over generators, 0, sums and scalar multiples). In particular it vanishes at y = x ∈ Q.

5. Conclusion. ξ(x)(ι_xβ) = ±(ι_xβ)(τ) = ±β(x, τ) = 0. As β was arbitrary, the conclusion holds at μ-a.e. x. The case n = 0 is included: then Q = span ∅ = {0} and x = 0. ∎

Implementation note. A complete Lean proof of this exact statement compiled during decomposition, using withDensity_absolutelyContinuous, Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le, dif_pos with Exists.choose_spec and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff, Submodule.span_induction, and ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq at positions 0 and b.succ.
proof_key_steps: μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M transfers `orients` to μ-a.e. x.
Uniqueness of approximate tangent planes identifies approxTangentPlane with the oriented plane Q, and p_Q x = x gives x ∈ Q.
y ↦ β(y, τ) is linear and vanishes on each τ_b (repeated entry), hence on Q ∋ x.
Therefore ξ(x)(ι_xβ) = ±β(x, τ) = 0 for every β.

subproblems.title: Cartan's formula for the Euler field X(x) = x
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let β : ℝ^P → Λ^{m+1}(ℝ^P) be an (m+1)-form differentiable at y. Let ι_Xβ be the m-form z ↦ β(z).curryLeft z, the contraction with the Euler field X(z) = z. Then
 d(ι_Xβ)(y) + ι_y(dβ(y)) = (m+1)·β(y) + Dβ(y)[y].
This is Cartan's formula L_X = dι_X + ι_X d for X(z) = z, with d the exterior derivative (Mathlib extDeriv), ι_y(dβ(y)) = (dβ(y)).curryLeft y, and Dβ(y) the Fréchet derivative.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (y : Euclid P), DifferentiableAt ℝ β y → exteriorDerivative (fun z => ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft (β z) z) y + ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft (exteriorDerivative β y) y = ((m : ℝ) + 1) • β y + fderiv ℝ β y y
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is the Cartan formula behind Simon's homotopy formula (Ch. 6, 2.25–2.26, chapter-06.txt lines 441–456) and Lemma 2.33 (lines 557–567), in the form used in step 6 of the parent proof: L_Xβ = d(ι_Xβ) + ι_X dβ for X(x) = x, where L_Xβ(y) = (m+1)β(y) + Dβ(y)[y] for an (m+1)-form β.

Conventions (Mathlib).
- dω(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dω(x)).
- alt := alternatizeUncurryFin satisfies (alt f)(v_0, …, v_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i f(v_i)(v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_k).
- (f.curryLeft x)(v) = f(x, v).
Let B := Dβ(y) = fderiv ℝ β y : ℝ^P →L Λ^{m+1}, and ψ(z) := β(z).curryLeft z.

1. Derivative of ψ. Φ(f, z) := f.curryLeft z is continuous and bilinear, since curryLeft is a linear isometry Λ^{m+1} → L(ℝ^P, Λ^m). Since ψ(z) = Φ(β(z), z) and β is differentiable at y, the product rule gives Dψ(y)[u] = (Bu).curryLeft y + β(y).curryLeft u. That is, Dψ(y) = K + β(y).curryLeft with K(u) := (Bu).curryLeft y.

2. dψ(y). By additivity of alt, dψ(y) = alt(Dψ(y)) = alt(K) + alt(β(y).curryLeft) = A + (m+1)β(y).
- Here A := alt(K), so A(v) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i (Bv_i)(y, v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_m).
- alt(f.curryLeft) = (m+1)f because Σ_i (−1)^i f(v_i, v_0, …, v̂_i, …) = Σ_i f(v): moving the i-th entry to the front is a cyclic permutation of sign (−1)^i (Mathlib alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft).

3. ι_y dβ(y). Let v = (v_0, …, v_m) and w := (y, v_0, …, v_m). Then dβ(y)(w) = Σ_{k=0}^{m+1} (−1)^k B(w_k)(w with w_k removed).
- The k = 0 term is B(y)(v).
- For k = i+1, removing entry i+1 of (y, v) leaves (y, v without v_i), so the term is (−1)^{i+1}(Bv_i)(y, v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_m).
Hence (dβ(y)).curryLeft y = B(y) − A.

4. Conclusion. Adding steps 2 and 3: dψ(y) + (dβ(y)).curryLeft y = A + (m+1)β(y) + B(y) − A = (m+1)·β(y) + Dβ(y)[y]. ∎

Implementation note. This exact statement was proved in Lean during decomposition (about 30 lines, standard axioms):
- ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt_of_bilinear with Φ := (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeftLI (n := m)).toContinuousLinearMap and hasFDerivAt_id;
- unfold exteriorDerivative and extDeriv; rewrite with alternatizeUncurryFin_add and alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft;
- ext v; alternatizeUncurryFin_apply; Fin.sum_univ_succ on the Fin (m+2) sum; Fin.removeNth_zero;
- the auxiliary identity Fin.removeNth i.succ (Matrix.vecCons y v) = Matrix.vecCons y (Fin.removeNth i v), proved by funext and Fin.cases with Fin.removeNth_apply and Fin.succ_succAbove_succ;
- finish with simp and ring.
proof_key_steps: Product rule: Dψ(y)u = (Dβ(y)u).curryLeft y + β(y).curryLeft u for ψ(z) = β(z).curryLeft z.
dψ(y) = alt(u ↦ (Dβ(y)u).curryLeft y) + (m+1)β(y), by alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft.
(dβ(y)).curryLeft y = Dβ(y)y − alt(u ↦ (Dβ(y)u).curryLeft y), by splitting off the k = 0 term.
Adding: d(ι_Xβ)(y) + ι_y dβ(y) = (m+1)β(y) + Dβ(y)[y].

subproblems.title: Cone criterion: ∂C = 0 and x ∧ C⃗ = 0 imply η_{0,λ#}C = C (Simon Lemma 6.2.33)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, n ≥ 1, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) with C = τ(M, θ, ξ) (R.Represents C). Assume ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C). Assume also x ∧ C⃗ = 0 μ_C-a.e., in the sense that for R.measure-a.e. x, ξ(x)(β.curryLeft x) = 0 for every (n+1)-covector β. Then C is a cone: currentEval(η_{0,λ#}C, ω) = C(ω) for every λ > 0 and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (IsConeCurrent C).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), 0 < n → R.Represents C → BoundaryVanishes C → (∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1), R.orient x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β x) = 0) → IsConeCurrent C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Sources.
- Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 2.33 and its proof (chapter-06.txt lines 557–567), via the homotopy formula 2.25–2.27 for the affine homotopy h(t, x) = tλ⁻¹x + (1 − t)x (lines 441–478), made explicit as in steps 6–7 of the parent proof.
- Simon 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt line 359): "hence we can apply Lemma 2.33 to deduce that C is a cone".
Simon's hypothesis M_{B_R(0)}(C) < ∞ is supplied by the integer multiplicity representation. Uses sibling euler_cartan (child 5).

Notation. Write n = m + 1 (n ≥ 1). M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, ν := Hⁿ⌞M and μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ. For a test form φ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), R.action φ = ∫_M θ ξ(φ) dHⁿ, and C(φ) = R.action φ because R.Represents C.

0. Preliminaries.
(a) ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for ν-a.e. x. By `orients`, ξ(x)(α) = ±α(τ) with τ orthonormal, and |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_i|τ_i| = ‖α‖.
(b) For φ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(φ(x)) is ν-integrable. It is AEStronglyMeasurable (θ measurable, ξ AEStronglyMeasurable, φ continuous, evaluation continuous bilinear). It is bounded by sup|φ|·θ·1_{tsupport φ}, and ∫_{M∩tsupport φ} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult.
(c) The hypothesis holds ν-a.e. θ is measurable and θ ≥ 1 on M, so (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Q x) ⟺ ∀ᵐ x ∂ν, (θ x ≠ 0 → Q x) (ae_withDensity_iff), and ν-a.e. x lies in M, where θ x ≠ 0.
(d) Linearity and boundary. C(φ₁ + φ₂) = C(φ₁) + C(φ₂) for φ₁, φ₂ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ. For ψ ∈ 𝒟^m, C(dψ) = (∂C)(ψ) = 0: BoundaryVanishes C means C.boundary = 0 (n = m+1), and C.boundary ψ = C(exteriorDerivativeTestOn ψ) = C(dψ).

1. Setup.
- Fix λ > 0 and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), and choose R_ω > 0 with tsupport ω ⊆ B̄_{R_ω}(0).
- Let c(s) := 1 + s(λ⁻¹ − 1) for s ∈ ℝ, so c(0) = 1, c(1) = λ⁻¹ and c' ≡ λ⁻¹ − 1. The set J := {s : c(s) > 0} is an open interval containing [0, 1].
- For s ∈ J let h_s(y) := c(s)y and β_s := h_s^#ω, that is, β_s(y)(v_1, …, v_n) := ω(c(s)y)(c(s)v_1, …, c(s)v_n) = c(s)ⁿω(c(s)y)(v). Equivalently, β_s(y) = (ω(c(s)y)).compContinuousLinearMap(c(s)·Id).
- β_s is smooth and tsupport β_s ⊆ c(s)⁻¹·tsupport ω, which is compact, so β_s ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Also β_0 = ω and β_1(y) = ω(λ⁻¹y)∘(λ⁻¹·).
- Put F(s) := R.action β_s = ∫_M θ ξ(β_s) dHⁿ, which equals C(β_s) for s ∈ J.

2. s-derivative. For fixed y, s ↦ β_s(y) ∈ Λⁿ is differentiable with ∂_sβ_s(y) = c'·[n c(s)^{n−1}ω(c(s)y) + c(s)ⁿDω(c(s)y)[y]]. Since Dβ_s(y)[u] = c(s)^{n+1}Dω(c(s)y)[u], this equals ∂_sβ_s(y) = (c'/c(s))·Lβ_s(y), where Lβ(y) := nβ(y) + Dβ(y)[y].

3. Differentiation under the integral sign. Fix s₀ ∈ J and δ > 0 with [s₀ − δ, s₀ + δ] ⊆ J, and let 0 < m₀ ≤ c(s) ≤ M₀ on this interval.
- For such s and all y, β_s(y) and ∂_sβ_s(y) vanish unless c(s)y ∈ tsupport ω, in particular unless |y| ≤ R_ω/m₀. (Dω vanishes off tsupport ω.)
- |∂_sβ_s(y)| ≤ |c'|(nM₀^{n−1}sup|ω| + M₀ⁿsup|Dω|R_ω/m₀) =: K; here ω and Dω are continuous with compact support.
- With (a), g(s,y) := θ(y)ξ(y)(β_s(y)) satisfies |∂_s g(s,y)| ≤ K·θ(y)·1_{B̄_{R_ω/m₀}(0)}(y) for ν-a.e. y and all such s. This bound is ν-integrable, and g(s₀,·) is ν-integrable by (b).
- By the dominated differentiation theorem (hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le), F is differentiable at s₀ with
 F'(s₀) = ∫_M θ ξ(∂_sβ_{s₀}) dHⁿ = (c'/c(s₀))·∫_M θ ξ(Lβ_{s₀}) dHⁿ.

4. Cartan. Let ψ(y) := β_{s₀}(y).curryLeft y (an m-form) and χ(y) := (dβ_{s₀}(y)).curryLeft y (an n-form).
- Both are smooth (compositions of smooth maps with continuous bilinear maps; dβ_{s₀} is smooth) and have tsupport ⊆ tsupport β_{s₀}. So ψ ∈ 𝒟^m, dψ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ and χ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ.
- By child 5 (with β := β_{s₀}, which is differentiable at every y), dψ(y) + χ(y) = (m+1)β_{s₀}(y) + Dβ_{s₀}(y)[y] = Lβ_{s₀}(y) for all y.
- Hence Lβ_{s₀} = dψ + χ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, and by (d), ∫_M θ ξ(Lβ_{s₀}) dHⁿ = C(Lβ_{s₀}) = C(dψ) + C(χ).

5. Both terms vanish.
- C(dψ) = 0 by (d), since ∂C = 0.
- C(χ) = ∫_M θ(y)ξ(y)((dβ_{s₀}(y)).curryLeft y) dHⁿ(y) = 0: apply the hypothesis with the (n+1)-covector dβ_{s₀}(y) and use (c); the integrand vanishes for ν-a.e. y.
Hence F'(s₀) = 0 for every s₀ ∈ J.

6. Constancy. F is differentiable on J ⊇ [0, 1] with zero derivative, so F(1) = F(0) by the mean value theorem. Here F(0) = C(β_0) = C(ω) and F(1) = C(β_1).

7. IsConeCurrent.
- For λ > 0, the map dilation 0 λ, y ↦ −λ⁻¹·0 + λ⁻¹y, is surjective: y = dilation 0 λ (λy). So tsupport ω ⊆ dilation 0 λ '' ℝ^P.
- Unfolding currentEval, blowUp, affinePushforward and restrictDomain gives currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(affinePullbackForm L b ω), with L = dilationCLM P λ = λ⁻¹·Id and b = −(λ⁻¹·0) = 0.
- affinePullbackForm L b ω (y) = (ω(b + Ly)).compContinuousLinearMap L = ω(λ⁻¹y)∘(λ⁻¹·) = β_1(y). (This unfolding was checked in Lean during decomposition.)
- Hence currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = F(1) = F(0) = C(ω) for every λ > 0 and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), i.e. IsConeCurrent C. ∎
